bull_bear.body:
- Long-established single destination: described as Gujarat's biggest one-stop entertainment hub, operating for more than 30 years and BSE-listed since 1994
- Promoter-led with an experienced promoter family: the Chairman & Managing Director has around 40 years of construction/real-estate experience and has run the amusement, water-park and resort business alongside it
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- No revenue from operations in the year under review — The Directors' Report states the Company generated no revenue from operation during the year as it proposed to diversify its business activities - the operating amusement/resort business effectively stopped contributing, leaving the year's result dependent on an exceptional item rather than trading.
- Diversification is announced but undefined — The proposed diversification of business activities is stated without naming a target business, an investment plan or a timeline, so there is no disclosed basis on which to judge execution, and the proceeds of the property sale are earmarked for it alongside debt repayment and capex.
- Disposal of the principal immovable property — The Company sold its immovable property at CTS number NA 62 and land admeasuring 69,973 sq mtrs bearing CTS number NA 63 (P) at Village Rayantal wadi, Taluka Waghodia, District Baroda. The land base underpinning a single-site amusement-park and resort operator is materially reduced by such a sale, and the registered office was itself shifted out of the Ajwa Nimeta Road compound during the year.
- Promoter / Promoter Group seeking reclassification to Public category — A post-year-end material change: the Company has received a request from the Promoters / Promoter Group to reclassify their shares from 'Promoter and Promoter Group' to 'Public', and the reclassification is under process - a structural change in who is accountable for the Company at the same time as the business is being repositioned.
- Key-man and family concentration at the top of the Company — The board skills matrix rests the Company on the promoter Chairman & Managing Director (promoter of the Ajwa Group, a real-estate developer of some 40 years' standing) and on Mr Rahil Jain, who is a relative of the Chairperson; the other directors are described in generic competency terms, with no disclosed successor or second line.
- Thin and disrupted independent-director bench — Mr Arvind Manubhai Vakil ceased to be an Independent Director on his death on 21 September 2025 and a replacement additional Independent Director was appointed only with effect from 12 January 2026, leaving the Audit, Nomination & Remuneration and Stakeholders' committees short of independent members for most of the year; the Audit Committee is described as comprising Independent Directors while also listing a non-executive director who is a relative of the Chairperson, and one independent director attended only one of the eight board meetings.
- Low dematerialisation of the share capital — As on 31 March 2026, 55.90% of the Company's total paid-up capital was in dematerialised form, leaving a large minority of the capital in physical form - a transferability and liquidity constraint for shareholders.
- No dividend and cash conservation — Directors did not recommend a dividend for the year under review in order to conserve the financial resources of the Company, so shareholder return depends entirely on the outcome of the pending diversification.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

outlook.body:
- Stay focused on the core recreation and hospitality segment rather than entering new formats
- Asset optimisation: focused maintenance and regular updates to the existing water-park attractions, event plots and food-and-beverage facilities
- Targeted regional marketing to expand local visibility and capture high-density footfalls from nearby metropolitan areas
- Strict cost containment across food, beverage and seasonal entertainment operations to protect margins against inflationary pressure
- Shorten the extended working-capital cycle by fast-tracking sluggish collection timelines and reducing high debtor days - stated as an active internal priority
- Selective facility upgrades and higher non-peak (mid-week / off-season) occupancy in the coming fiscal, including diversifying through mid-week bundles
- Upgrade water-saving and recycling technology as the stated management action against volatile utility and energy costs
- Diversify the business: the Company generated no revenue from operations during the year as it proposed to diversify its business activities, with the proceeds of the property sale earmarked partly for that diversification
- Leverage the debt-free / low-leverage balance sheet to improve liquidity patterns and maximise long-term shareholder value
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: No new capacity addition, project or commissioning timeline is disclosed. Capital activity in FY26 ran the other way: the Company disposed of its immovable property at CTS number NA 62 and land admeasuring 69,973 sq mtrs bearing CTS number NA 63 (P) at Village Rayantal wadi, Taluka Waghodia, District Baroda, stating the sale was to optimise the asset portfolio and meet business and financial requirements, with proceeds to be utilised towards repayment of borrowings, capital expenditure and diversification of business. On the existing estate the stated vector is asset optimisation - focused maintenance and regular updates to the existing water-park attractions, event plots and food-and-beverage facilities - rather than expansion. For the coming year management says it targets selective facility upgrades and higher non-peak occupancy, and lists upgrading water-saving / recycling technology as a management action; no rupee quantum, project name or completion date is attached to any of these.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Micro-vacations growth - rising demand for short weekend getaways and highway tourism near Tier-2 urban hubs
- Consumer preference for integrated destinations combining amusement parks, water sports and themed resort cottages under a single operational footprint
- Regional hub traction across primary tourist corridors in Western India, driven by local corporate outings, wedding events and family-oriented weekend traffic
- Rising disposable income in Tier-2/3 towns is the stated opportunity; intense competition from local options is the stated threat
- Expansion of the corporate-events and weddings segment as an incremental demand pool
- Revenue volatility: shifting quarterly top-line performance heavily influenced by weather changes and off-season shifts in public recreational spending, plus high reliance on peak holiday seasons
- Margins constrained by fixed overheads - park maintenance and employee expenses - which limited near-term profit growth
- Climatic shifts such as delayed monsoons flagged as a threat to the season
- Balance sheet described as fundamentally robust with minimal long-term debt and low leverage risk
